title: Sorting the Sentence
summary: A sentence consists of words separated by a single space, with no leading or trailing spaces.
statement: A sentence consists of words separated by a single space, with no leading or trailing spaces. Words are made up of lowercase and uppercase English letters. Shuffling involves appending the word's 1-indexed position to each word and then rearranging the words. For a sentence with no more than 9 words, the original sentence is to be reconstructed from a shuffled version.
constraints: Each shuffled word ends in its unique one-based position digit; there are at most nine words.
Remove digits and return the words in original order separated by spaces.
hints: The final character of each word is its destination position.
Allocate an output list and place the word without its digit at index digit-1.
Join the filled positions with single spaces.
Position suffixes are unique and cover every slot, so direct placement reconstructs the original ordering exactly.
editorial: Position suffixes are unique and cover every slot, so direct placement reconstructs the original ordering exactly.

tests.explanation: Positions 1-4 restore This is a sentence.
The suffix digits restore Me Myself and I.
